title: Unmeasured fidelity renders UNKNOWN — the panel's integrity row stops claiming a score it never observed
status_note: Describes what happened (Law 3). All three brief work items were implemented and each is pinned by a test that was DEMONSTRATED failing against the pre-fix source before being demonstrated passing against the fixed one. Two additional tests were added beyond the brief's three because the feeder trace demanded them (see findings FID-F4) and because all three brief tests SKIP on the dev interpreter, which would have left the invariant unenforced in CI (see method.why_two_instruments). Two of my own source-pin assertions were wrong on first run and were corrected in the TEST, never by weakening the code. memory/agent_state.py was not touched. No styling was changed beyond the neutral UNKNOWN state.

method.why_two_instruments: gate_widget.py hard-imports PySide at module top, so every behavioural test of this row SKIPS on the dev interpreter — and a skip exits 0, which CI reads as passing. That is the Law-1 failure mode: a check that cannot run is a decoration that will be cited as evidence. So the contract is pinned twice: behaviourally under hython (real QWidgets, no stubs) and structurally by a Qt-free ast source-pin that executes on EVERY interpreter. This mirrors the house's existing answer to the same problem, tests/test_panel_fidelity_honesty_sourcepin.py.

findings.claim: The integrity row was CONSTRUCTED claiming a perfect score. The label was the literal string "Fidelity 1.0" and the dot was hardcoded to the green success token, both before a single operation had been observed.
findings.anchor: pre-fix python/synapse/panel/gate_widget.py:388 (label) and :383-385 (t.GROW dot), at commit 1f18ab46.
findings.fix: python/synapse/panel/gate_widget.py:475-488 — neither the dot colour nor the label text is named at construction; both are seeded by _render_fidelity(None), so the row is born UNKNOWN and cannot be constructed into a state it never observed.

findings.claim: The update path fabricated a default on the way in and formatted it unconditionally. `report.get("session_fidelity", 1.0)` turned an ABSENT measurement into a perfect one, and there was no UNKNOWN branch anywhere on the update path.
findings.anchor: pre-fix python/synapse/panel/gate_widget.py:583 (the defaulted get) and :598 (the unconditional format).
findings.fix: The default is gone: :697 reads through _observed_fidelity(report) (:73), which returns None — never a number — when the report is not a dict, when the key is absent, when the value is not a real number, or when operations_total is present and zero. :701 renders through _render_fidelity, which delegates the colour to _fidelity_color (:114) so green cannot be reached without passing the unmeasured guard.
findings.pinned_by: id-c + test_no_defaulted_get_on_session_fidelity, which fails on ANY two-argument .get("session_fidelity", ...) — there is no honest default for an unmade measurement, so the pin rejects 0.0 as firmly as 1.0.

findings.claim: update_integrity had ZERO test coverage before this leg. Not a check that could not fail — no check at all. That is why a fabricated perfect score survived in a widget whose entire job is to report honesty.
findings.anchor: Producer: grep -rn "update_integrity|_fidelity_label|_fidelity_dot" --include=*.py tests/  ->  no matches at commit 1f18ab46.

findings.claim: THE FIX AS LITERALLY BRIEFED WOULD HAVE CHANGED NOTHING ON THE LIVE PATH. shared/bridge.py:2834's session_fidelity property returns a clean 1.0 when operations_total == 0, and session_report() (:2842) always includes the key. So on the live WebSocket path (chat_panel.py:233 -> ws_bridge.py:322 -> handle_ws_report) the key is never absent — removing this widget's .get default would simply have moved the fabricated perfect score upstream instead of removing it. The visible lie would have been identical.
findings.disposition: Handled inside _observed_fidelity: operations_total == 0 is treated as unmeasured. This is NOT new policy — it is the already-ratified `has_data` doctrine from session_integrity.py:138-142 and integrity_readout.py:47-48, applied to this row. Absent operations_total is deliberately NOT treated as zero; only a positively-disqualifying zero suppresses. Escalated as FID-R1 because the upstream half is not mine to change.
findings.pinned_by: test_zero_operations_is_unknown_not_the_bridges_resting_one, with test_a_measured_session_still_reaches_green as its negative control — proving the guard suppresses the rest state without suppressing genuine greens.

findings.claim: Two of this leg's own source-pin assertions were WRONG on first run and are recorded rather than quietly fixed. (a) The literal-score detector flagged the legitimate format template "Fidelity {f:.1f}" because it contains a digit; the tell is a digit with NO placeholder, since nothing can substitute into it. (b) A vacuity-control assertion tested line ordering rather than the property that actually bites, and would have passed on the bad source it was meant to reject.
findings.anchor: First run: 2 failed, 7 passed. Both were corrected IN THE TEST — the code under test was not weakened to accommodate either (Law 6). The corrected controls now include a positive case proving the template is not flagged.
findings.why_recorded: The first status was wrong. A receipt that only reports the run where everything worked is the same defect this leg was dispatched to remove.

findings.claim: The same claim-without-observation class survives in the OTHER TWO CELLS of this row. operations_total and anchor_violations still carry fabricated .get(..., 0) defaults, and the row is constructed reading "0 ops" / "0 violations" before anything is observed. By the governing law's own words — a zero is a claim — those are the identical defect in the quieter direction.
findings.why_not_fixed: The brief scopes the work to fidelity and forbids styling redesign beyond the neutral UNKNOWN state. Widening scope is not mine to decide (Article I). Escalated as FID-R2.

for_ruling.question: shared/bridge.py:2834 returns a fabricated 1.0 at operations_total == 0 and session_report() always emits the key, so the rest state travels to every consumer as if it were a measurement (FID-F4). Does the producer become honest — Optional[float], or an explicit has_data field on session_report() — or is the consumer-side guard the permanent answer?
for_ruling.why_it_needs_a_human: Article I. shared/bridge.py is deny-listed from agent edit, and changing a public property's return type is an interface decision with three known consumers, not something provable from the tree.
for_ruling.evidence_offered: There are now THREE independent consumer-side re-derivations of the same guard: session_integrity.py:113 (has_data), integrity_readout.py:47 (has_data), and gate_widget.py:73 (operations_total <= 0). Each was written separately, which is the signal that the honesty belongs upstream — but also the signal that the existing house answer has been consumer-side twice already.
for_ruling.recommendation: Do not change the property in this leg's wake. Consider a single shared helper so a fourth consumer does not have to rediscover it.

for_ruling.question: FID-F6 — operations_total and anchor_violations still default to 0 and are constructed as "0 ops" / "0 violations" before anything is observed. By the governing law (a zero is a claim) that is the same defect. Extend UNKNOWN to those two cells?
for_ruling.why_it_needs_a_human: The brief scoped this leg to fidelity and explicitly forbade styling changes beyond the neutral UNKNOWN state. Extending the treatment changes what two more cells say at rest — a product-surface judgement, not a provable fact.
for_ruling.scope_note: Cheap if approved: both already route through the same row and the helpers generalise. The pins would be the same shape as id-a/id-c.

for_ruling.question: update_integrity early-returns on a falsy report (gate_widget.py:694-695), so a None or empty session_report leaves the previously rendered value standing. Is a last-observed value that no longer describes the current payload acceptable, or should a falsy report also reset the row to UNKNOWN?
for_ruling.why_it_needs_a_human: Defensible both ways and left UNCHANGED deliberately. I judged a last-observed value to be honest (it was measured, and nothing fabricates it) rather than stale-as-current; at rest the row is UNKNOWN either way, so no fabrication is reachable through this path today. Recording the judgement rather than burying it.
